{"labels":["minion-proposal","minion-failed","minion-research-completed","minion-reviewed"],"n":4,"state":"OPEN","title":"Resolve checkpoint metadata from fork PRs"}
- Returns per-ID outcomes so the command can build the summary counts.

**Commit shape.** One single-parent commit per run on `partio/checkpoints/v1`, parented on the current local tip. The fork's history is never a parent. Message `sync-fork: <owner>/<repo>#<n> (<k> checkpoints)`, body listing the synced IDs and the head repo `full_name`. No commit when zero checkpoints were added. Provenance lives only in the commit message. The `metadata.json` schema is unchanged. The configured git identity is used as-is.

**Branch initialisation.** Move the orphan-branch creation (empty tree → parentless `commit-tree "partio: initialize checkpoint storage"` → `update-ref`) out of `enable` into a shared helper in the checkpoint package, used by both `enable` and `sync-fork`. `sync-fork` calls it only when the branch is missing **and** at least one checkpoint will be written.

**Outcomes and exit codes.**
- Exit 0 with a one-line reason: same-repo PR (`head.repo.full_name == base.repo.full_name`); deleted fork (null or missing `head.repo`, or empty `clone_url`, all treated alike); fork has no `partio/checkpoints/v1`; no valid trailers.
- Exit 0 with warnings: IDs missing from the fork, conflicts, more than 250 commits, base repo differing from the owner/repo parsed from `git remote get-url origin`.
- Non-zero: unparseable reference, API/auth/rate-limit errors, fetch errors other than an absent branch, corrupt local branch, failed ref update.
- Every run that reaches the sync prints `synced N, already present M, conflicts C, missing K`, plus the PR's `base.repo.full_name` and the 250-commit gap when it applies.

**Workflow template (`.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml.example`).**
- Trigger: `pull_request_target`, types `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`. Job condition: `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork`.
- Permissions: `contents: write`, `pull-requests: read`.
- `actions/checkout` of the base repository only, never `ref: head.sha`. Fork content is fetched as git objects and read as data, never checked out or executed.
- `actions/setup-go`, then `go install github.com/partio-io/cli/cmd/partio@${PARTIO_VERSION}`, where `PARTIO_VERSION` is one env var at the top of the file, set to the first release that ships `sync-fork`. Never `@latest`.
- Set a bot identity (`github-actions[bot]` name/email) before syncing.
- If `git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/partio/checkpoints/v1` succeeds, fetch it into the local branch. Otherwise proceed without it. No `|| true` masking.
- Run `partio sync-fork "${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}"` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`.
- Push with `git push origin partio/checkpoints/v1`, never forced. On rejection, re-fetch origin's branch, re-run `sync-fork` (idempotent), and push again, up to 3 attempts. After that the job fails visibly.
- `concurrency`: a fixed group (e.g. `partio-checkpoints`), `cancel-in-progress: false`, `queue: max`. A comment notes that GHES lacks `queue` and the retry loop is the safeguard there.
- Header comment: on public repositories GitHub's default Actions event policy blocks `pull_request_target` (enforced from 2026-12-02). The maintainer must add an event policy that explicitly allows it for this workflow, or use the manual command path.
- The `.example` suffix keeps it inert in this repository. Workflow files must end in `.yml`/`.yaml` to run.

**Docs.** A README "Fork contributions" section with four parts: (1) contributor requirements (`push_sessions` true, which is the default; not stealth mode; push to the fork); (2) maintainer setup (copy the template to `.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml`, set `PARTIO_VERSION`, add the `pull_request_target` allow policy on public repos, the permissions used and why `pull_request_target` is safe here); (3) the manual alternative (`partio sync-fork <pr-url>` then `git push origin partio/checkpoints/v1`); (4) the reviewer flow (fetch the upstream branch, run `partio explain <id>` from the trailer) with the non-fast-forward case on a diverged local branch stated as a known limitation. Mention that #532/#624 may change where contributors push. Add a `partio sync-fork <pr>` row to the command table.

**Delivery.** Three slices, each its own reviewable change:
1. Happy path end-to-end: reference parsing, the `Client.Do` empty-token fix, PR/commit API calls, trailer extraction, fork fetch to a unique temporary ref with cleanup, validated subtree import with skip-if-present, the single sync commit, the shared branch-init extraction (used by `enable`), summary output, and tests.
2. Edge outcomes: conflicts, deleted fork, missing fork branch, the 250-commit warning, the origin-mismatch warning, and the full summary counts, with tests.
3. Workflow template (identity setup, `PARTIO_VERSION` pin, concurrency, push retry, policy header) plus the README section and command-table row.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here exercises observable behaviour, such as branch contents, refs, exit outcomes, and summary counts, through real git repositories in `t.TempDir()` and a local `httptest.Server`. Tests do not mock git. No test touches the network: fork clone URLs are `file://` paths to temp repos, and the API root is pointed at the test server through `GITHUB_API_URL` set with `t.Setenv`. Standard library `testing` only, table-driven where there are several cases.

Modules and cases:

- **PR reference parser**: valid URL forms, including trailing `/files` and `/commits`; `owner/repo#n`; rejects such as a missing number, a non-numeric number, an issue URL, and a bare number. The usage error names both forms.
- **Trailer extractor**: several trailers in the final block; key case variations; a `---` line in the body; a trailer-like line in an earlier paragraph (ignored); invalid IDs (warned and skipped); duplicates across commits (deduped, first-seen order).
- **`internal/github` client**: `Do` sends `Authorization` with a token and omits it with an empty token (table-driven); the PR GET and paginated commit listing decode the new type; a rate-limit status yields the "set `GH_TOKEN`" error. Prior art: the existing `client_test.go` and `pages_test.go`.
- **Checkpoint import**: rejects a subtree with a symlink, a gitlink, or an executable entry; rejects a missing `metadata.json` and a mismatched ID; same-hash skip; different-hash conflict leaves upstream untouched; imported subtree hash equals the fork's. Prior art: the checkpoint package's existing store/prune tests, which build branches with plumbing in temp repos.
- **Branch-init helper**: creates the orphan branch; `enable` still behaves as before.
- **Command integration**: a "fork" repo with real checkpoints written by `Store.Write` and a separate "upstream" repo; the `httptest` server serves PR and commits JSON whose `head.repo.clone_url` is the fork's `file://` path. Assert that exactly the referenced checkpoints land upstream; that `checkpoint.Read` resolves them; that a second run creates no commit; that a conflicting ID is not overwritten; that the temporary ref is gone after both a successful and a failing run; that the fork's `show-ref` output is byte-identical before and after (the read-only guarantee); and that the nothing-to-do cases exit 0 with their reason while real failures exit non-zero. Prior art: `cmd/partio/rewind_test.go` and `internal/hooks/postcommit_test.go`, which set up temp repos with an initialised checkpoint branch.

Any helper that only tests use, such as a test override of the API root, a fixed temporary-ref name, or a fixture builder, lives in a `_test.go` file of its package, not in production code, even where existing prior art puts such helpers in production code.

## Out of Scope

- Changing `partio explain` or `checkpoint.Read`, including any fallback lookup across remotes or network access from `explain`.
- A GitHub App integration.
- Changing which remote the contributor-side pre-push targets (covered by #532 and #624).
- A `--push` flag or any push performed by the command itself.
- Any write to the fork.
- A git-history fallback for PRs with more than 250 commits.
- A size cap on imported checkpoint data.
- Cross-checking `metadata.commit_hash` against PR commits.
- Changes to the `metadata.json` schema, including provenance fields.
- A merge or force workaround for reviewers whose local checkpoint branch has diverged.
- Cutting the release that ships `sync-fork` and filling in `PARTIO_VERSION` (a human step).
- Enabling the workflow in any real repository, and creating the `pull_request_target` event policy (maintainer decisions).
- Skipping already-published research artifacts on re-runs (unrelated pipeline behaviour).

## Further Notes

- **Untrusted data, no size cap.** Fork checkpoints are validated for structure and ID but not for size. A fork can upload a large session blob, and the sync will copy it into the upstream object database. This is an accepted v1 trade-off: the maintainer, or the workflow they enabled, controls whether the result is pushed.
- **`pull_request_target` default policy deadline.** GitHub's default Actions event policy blocks `pull_request_target` on public repositories. It is in evaluate mode now and enforced from 2026-12-02, about two weeks after this research run. Without an explicit allow policy the template never runs on a public upstream. Private and internal repositories are not affected. The manual command stays the fallback.
- **`queue: max` is github.com/GHEC only.** On GHES the default `queue: single` behaviour can cancel a pending sync when a newer one queues. The push-retry loop is the safeguard there, but a dropped run still means that PR's checkpoints sync only on its next push or a manual run.
- **Unchecked risk: deleted-fork API shape.** No source confirmed that GitHub returns `head.repo: null` for a deleted fork. The REST schema and webhook payload list `head.repo` as required and not nullable (Evidence: none found). The implementation therefore treats a null `head.repo`, a missing `head.repo`, and an empty `clone_url` alike, rather than relying on one exact shape.
- **Private forks.** The fetch relies on the fork's checkpoint branch being readable with the credentials available to git. Public forks are readable anonymously (verified). Private forks may need credentials the Actions token does not grant. That case was not investigated.
- **Trailer block rule.** Only the final trailer block of a message is parsed. `AmendTrailers` always appends one final paragraph, so Partio-written commits are covered. A hand-edited message that moves the trailer into an earlier paragraph will not be detected, by design.
- **Contributor side.** Contributors in stealth mode (`push_sessions: false`) never push the checkpoint branch, so there is nothing to sync. That is a nothing-to-do exit 0, not an error.
- **Rate limits.** Unauthenticated runs are capped at 60 requests/hour per IP. Each run makes at least two calls, the PR GET and one or more commit pages.

## Proposed slices

### Slice 1 — Add `partio sync-fork` to copy a fork PR's checkpoints into the local checkpoint branch

An upstream maintainer runs `partio sync-fork https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` (or `<owner>/<repo>#<n>`). The command parses the reference, asks the GitHub API for the PR's head repository and head commits, reads the `Partio-Checkpoint` trailers from those commits, fetches the fork's `partio/checkpoints/v1` into a temporary ref unique to this run, and copies only the referenced checkpoints into the local `partio/checkpoints/v1` in one single-parent commit. After the sync, `partio explain <id>` resolves the fork checkpoint like a local one. The command never writes to the fork and never pushes.

The walking skeleton does the whole path safely. Each copied checkpoint is validated: it is a tree; its `metadata.json` blob parses as `Metadata` and its ID equals the trailer ID; every entry, recursively, is a `100644` blob or a `040000` tree. The fork's subtree object is grafted unchanged, so its tree hash is identical to the fork's. Before grafting, the existing `getCheckpointTreeHash` helper looks up the ID in the local tree. A matching hash means already present, skipped silently. A different hash means a conflict: the command warns and keeps the upstream copy. This check belongs in this slice because `addToTree` does not dedupe names, and grafting over an existing ID would build a shard with duplicate entries. An ID absent from the fork tree counts as missing and gets a warning. When nothing new was copied, no commit is written. Every run prints `synced N, already present M, conflicts C, missing K`.

The orphan-branch creation moves out of `createCheckpointBranch` in `cmd/partio/enable.go` into a shared helper in `internal/checkpoint`, for example `checkpoint.InitBranch`. `enable` calls it in place of its current code, and `sync-fork` calls it only when the branch is missing and at least one checkpoint will be written. `github.Client.Do` sends the `Authorization` header only when `Token` is non-empty, so public repositories work without a token. The token comes from `GH_TOKEN`, then `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the API root comes from `GITHUB_API_URL` (default `https://api.github.com`). The host in the PR URL is never used.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `partio sync-fork <url>` accepts `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>`, with trailing segments such as `/files` or `/commits` tolerated, and `<owner>/<repo>#<n>`; owner, repo and number come only from the URL path, and any other form (issue URL, bare number, missing or non-numeric number) fails with a usage error that shows both forms
- [ ] A new PR-reference parser in its own file in `cmd/partio/` is called by the `sync-fork` command and covered by table-driven tests
- [ ] `github.Client.Do` omits the `Authorization` header when `Token` is empty and sends `Bearer <token>` otherwise (table-driven test in `client_test.go`)
- [ ] New `internal/github` calls in their own file — a single-PR GET and a paginated `pulls/{n}/commits` listing through `GetPages` — decode a new response type with `head.repo.full_name`, `head.repo.clone_url`, `head.sha` and `base.repo.full_name` (with `head.repo` a pointer, so a null value decodes without a panic); the existing `PullRequest` type is unchanged, and `sync-fork` calls both new functions
- [ ] A trailer extractor in its own file passes each commit message on stdin to `git interpret-trailers --parse --no-divider`, matches the `Partio-Checkpoint` key case-insensitively, keeps only `^[0-9a-f]{12}$` values, warns once per rejected value, and dedupes in first-seen order; its tests cover several trailers, key case, a `---` line in the body, a trailer-like line in an earlier paragraph (ignored), and invalid and duplicate values
- [ ] The fork branch is fetched with `git fetch --no-tags <clone_url> +refs/heads/partio/checkpoints/v1:<tmp-ref>` into a per-run unique ref outside `refs/heads/` (for example `refs/partio/sync-fork/<random>`), deleted with `update-ref -d` in deferred cleanup that runs on success and on error
- [ ] A new `Store` method in its own file in `internal/checkpoint`, called by `sync-fork`, rejects a subtree that contains a symlink, a gitlink or an executable, or that lacks `metadata.json`, or whose metadata ID differs from the trailer ID; it grafts accepted subtrees with an unchanged tree hash and returns a per-ID outcome (synced, already present, conflict, missing)
- [ ] A checkpoint that already exists locally with the same tree hash is skipped silently; one with a different hash is warned about, counted as a conflict, and left untouched upstream
- [ ] All new checkpoints from one run land in one commit parented only on the current local tip, with message `sync-fork: <owner>/<repo>#<n> (<k> checkpoints)` and a body listing the synced IDs and the head repo `full_name`; the configured git identity is used, and the fork's history is never a parent
- [ ] When zero checkpoints are added, no commit is written and no branch is created
- [ ] `checkpoint.InitBranch` (or the equivalent shared helper) creates the parentless `partio: initialize checkpoint storage` commit and ref; `enable` calls it in place of its own copy, and `sync-fork` calls it only when the branch is missing and at least one checkpoint will be written; existing `enable` tests still pass
- [ ] The command prints `synced N, already present M, conflicts C, missing K` on every run that reaches the sync
- [ ] An integration test uses a temp "fork" repo with checkpoints written by `Store.Write`, a separate temp "upstream" repo, and an `httptest.Server` reached through `GITHUB_API_URL` (set with `t.Setenv`) whose `head.repo.clone_url` is the fork's `file://` path. It asserts that exactly the referenced checkpoints land upstream, that `checkpoint.Read` resolves them, that a second run writes no commit, that a conflicting ID is not overwritten, that no ref under `refs/partio/sync-fork/` remains after a successful run or a failing one, and that the fork's `git show-ref` output is byte-identical before and after
- [ ] Any test-only fixture builder or helper lives in a `_test.go` file; production code has no test override hooks
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass

#### Modules touched

- cmd/partio (new `sync-fork` command, PR-reference parser, trailer extractor, registration in `main.go`, `enable.go` switched to the shared branch-init helper)
- internal/github (`Client.Do` empty-token fix, new PR and PR-commits calls and response type)
- internal/checkpoint (validated subtree import `Store` method, sync commit, shared branch-init helper)

#### Out of scope

- Clean exit-0 outcomes for a same-repo PR, a deleted fork, a fork with no checkpoint branch, and no valid trailers; the 250-commit warning; the origin-mismatch warning; the rate-limit hint (Slice 2). In this slice a deleted fork or a missing fork branch ends with a non-zero error, never a panic and never a partial write
- Workflow template and README (Slice 3)
- Any change to `partio explain` or `checkpoint.Read`; a `--push` flag; any write to the fork; a size cap; cross-checking `metadata.commit_hash`

### Slice 2 — Make `sync-fork` exit cleanly on nothing-to-do PRs and warn on partial or suspicious syncs

`sync-fork` now tells a real failure from a PR that simply has nothing to sync, so CI never goes red because a contributor does not use Partio. Four cases exit 0 after printing a one-line reason, before any fetch or write. The first is a same-repo PR, where `head.repo.full_name` equals `base.repo.full_name`. The second is a deleted fork: a null or missing `head.repo` or an empty `clone_url`, all treated alike. The third is a fork with no `partio/checkpoints/v1`, which `git ls-remote` against the clone URL detects before fetching, so the command never parses fetch error text. The fourth is a PR whose commits carry no valid `Partio-Checkpoint` trailer.

The command also warns when the result may be incomplete or surprising. A PR with more than 250 commits gets a warning, repeated in the summary, saying that commits beyond the first 250 were not scanned. The count comes from the single-PR GET's `commits` field, because the list endpoint returns null for it. A PR whose `base.repo.full_name` differs from the owner/repo parsed from `git remote get-url origin` gets a warning, not a failure, and the summary shows the base repository. A 403 or 429 rate-limit response becomes an error that tells the user to set `GH_TOKEN`. With no token, the command logs at debug level that requests are unauthenticated (60/hour).

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A same-repo PR exits 0 with a one-line reason and makes no fetch and no write
- [ ] A PR whose `head.repo` is null or missing, or whose `clone_url` is empty, exits 0 with a one-line "fork deleted" reason
- [ ] When `git ls-remote` shows that the fork has no `refs/heads/partio/checkpoints/v1`, the command exits 0 with a one-line reason, runs no fetch, and leaves no temporary ref
- [ ] A PR whose commits carry no valid checkpoint trailer exits 0 with a one-line reason
- [ ] Fetch errors other than an absent branch, a corrupt local branch, and a failed ref update still exit non-zero
- [ ] The PR response type gains the `commits` count; when it is above 250, the command prints a warning and the summary states that the commits after the first 250 were not scanned
- [ ] When the PR's `base.repo.full_name` differs from the owner/repo parsed from `origin`'s URL, the command prints a warning, still syncs, and shows the base repository in the summary; the origin-URL parser it adds is called from `sync-fork` in this slice
- [ ] A 403/429 rate-limit response from the GitHub API produces an error that names `GH_TOKEN` (covered in `internal/github` tests with an `httptest.Server`); with no token set, a debug log line says requests are unauthenticated
- [ ] Integration tests cover each exit-0 case, the 250-commit warning, the origin-mismatch warning, and a non-zero real failure, using temp repos and `httptest` only, with no network access
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass

#### Modules touched

- cmd/partio (`sync-fork` outcome handling, origin-URL owner/repo parsing, summary extensions)
- internal/github (`commits` field on the PR response type, rate-limit error mapping)

#### Out of scope

- A git-history fallback for PRs with more than 250 commits

- **Trailer block rule.** Only the final trailer block of a message is parsed. `AmendTrailers` always appends one final paragraph, so Partio-written commits are covered. A hand-edited message that moves the trailer into an earlier paragraph will not be detected, by design.
- **Contributor side.** Contributors in stealth mode (`push_sessions: false`) never push the checkpoint branch, so there is nothing to sync. That is a nothing-to-do exit 0, not an error.
- **Rate limits.** Unauthenticated runs are capped at 60 requests/hour per IP. Each run makes at least two calls, the PR GET and one or more commit pages.

### Slice 1 — Add `partio sync-fork` to copy a fork PR's checkpoints into the local checkpoint branch

An upstream maintainer runs `partio sync-fork https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` (or `<owner>/<repo>#<n>`). The command parses the reference, asks the GitHub API for the PR's head repository and head commits, reads the `Partio-Checkpoint` trailers from those commits, fetches the fork's `partio/checkpoints/v1` into a temporary ref unique to this run, and copies only the referenced checkpoints into the local `partio/checkpoints/v1` in one single-parent commit. After the sync, `partio explain <id>` resolves the fork checkpoint like a local one. The command never writes to the fork and never pushes.

The walking skeleton does the whole path safely. Each copied checkpoint is validated: it is a tree; its `metadata.json` blob parses as `Metadata` and its ID equals the trailer ID; every entry, recursively, is a `100644` blob or a `040000` tree. The fork's subtree object is grafted unchanged, so its tree hash is identical to the fork's. Before grafting, the existing `getCheckpointTreeHash` helper looks up the ID in the local tree. A matching hash means already present, skipped silently. A different hash means a conflict: the command warns and keeps the upstream copy. This check belongs in this slice because `addToTree` does not dedupe names, and grafting over an existing ID would build a shard with duplicate entries. An ID absent from the fork tree counts as missing and gets a warning. When nothing new was copied, no commit is written. Every run prints `synced N, already present M, conflicts C, missing K`.

The orphan-branch creation moves out of `createCheckpointBranch` in `cmd/partio/enable.go` into a shared helper in `internal/checkpoint`, for example `checkpoint.InitBranch`. `enable` calls it in place of its current code, and `sync-fork` calls it only when the branch is missing and at least one checkpoint will be written. `github.Client.Do` sends the `Authorization` header only when `Token` is non-empty, so public repositories work without a token.   since 2026-09-29 was `skipped`.
- **What happened.** Slice 1 added `sanitizeWindowsPath`, a helper that
  only its own test called, for slice 3. Slice 2 was green and did not
  touch it, but the guard failed slice 2. The exemption by plan name
  (`Plan.NamedAfter`) did not apply, because the plan did not name the
  helper. The failure text said "This slice wrote a duplicate", which
  was false. The fix session got only that text, made no edit, and
  stopped at its turn limit (`error_max_turns`).
- **The root cause, from jcleira (2026-10-18):** the plan was
  horizontal. Slice 1 added a package that "no existing code calls into
  yet". His rule: a slice does not add a function that it does not use.
  If a plan must do that, a reviewer catches it later.
- **Fix 1, live:** https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/780, merged
  2026-10-19 06:14Z. The slicer and the implement agent get the
  vertical rule, and the slicer checks its plan before it posts it. A
  change to a cli program takes effect on merge.
- **Fix 2, not live:** https://github.com/partio-io/minions/pull/148,
  merged 2026-10-19 06:14Z (merge `f9bb6bf`). The guard fails on unused
  earlier code only at the last slice, and before that slice it only
  logs a warning. `Plan.NamedAfter` is gone. The fix needs a release
  after v0.0.14 and a pin bump in all 8 cli workflows. That release
  also carries https://github.com/partio-io/minions/pull/147. The
  release steps: [[reference_partio_minions_deploy_chain]].
- **cli#55 waits.** On 2026-10-19 06:16Z nobody had started it again.
  Do not comment `/minion build` alone: the branch
  `minion/implement-implement-55` holds the slice 1 marker of the old
  plan, so the build continues at slice 2 and fails in the same way.
  The steps, each on his yes: delete that branch, comment
  `/minion research`, read the new plan, then comment `/minion build`.

## 2026-10-24 — cli#55: a wrong feature, two research fixes, two failed builds

From the session 976eb920 in `workspace-minion-reboot` (2026-10-19 to
2026-10-24 06:34Z). The live notes of the case are in the memory of
that workspace: `minions_research_outside_facts.md`,
`minions_gate_concurrency_cancels_pending.md`,
`feedback_work_the_minion_not_its_output.md` and
`minions_slice_plan_contract.md`.

- **Build 1 passed, but the feature was wrong.** The new plan had 2
  vertical slices, and
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/39259414444 (v0.0.14)
  built both with no fix session:
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/781. The review on 10-20 found
  two wrong facts about Claude Code. #781 searched
  `%APPDATA%\Claude\projects`, the folder of Claude Desktop; Claude
  Code keeps its sessions in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects`. Claude
  Code changes each character that is not a letter or a digit to `-`,
  but `sanitizeWindowsPath` changed only `\`, `:` and `/`. Research
  took the folder from the issue text and the spelling from partio's
  `sanitizePath`, and checked neither. The Linux `sanitizePath`
  (`internal/agent/claude/claude.go:20`) has the same spelling bug,
  outside #55.
- **His rule, 2026-10-23:** "we are not meant to be fixing generated PR
  issues here, why we would do that?". It was the second time, after
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/723 on 09-24. A review of a
  generated PR ends in a pipeline fix and a re-run. Never offer to
  repair the PR by hand. #781 was closed with no merge.
- **Research fix 1:** https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/788, merged
  10-23. The researcher writes an `Evidence:` line for each fact about
  an outside program. The next run,
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/39932494031, read
  https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/620, which uses `%USERPROFILE%`,
  and still kept `%APPDATA%`. Its evidence was the issue text.
- **Research fix 2:** https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/789, merged
  10-23. A `fact-checker` agent runs between the researcher and the
  persona. Its prompt names no fact of #55, so a run on #55 is a fair
  test. https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/39981700985 gave
  the correct folder and the full spelling rule, for about $3.20. The
  fact-checker alone cost $1.25 and used 46 turns with `max_turns: 40`.
  The plan:
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/issues/55#issuecomment-6369225998.
- **Build 2 stopped before any slice:**
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/40063785707. `Mark
  done` closed #55 on 10-19 when it opened #781, and the review gate
  refuses a closed issue. The fix,
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/pull/792 (open, CI green on 10-24),
  posts a comment and does not close the issue. The re-run steps:
  [[reference_partio_minions_deploy_chain]].
- **Build 3 failed at slice 2 of 2:**
  https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/40066394625. The plan
  asked for an unexported `resetCache()` for tests, and slice 1 put it
  in `internal/wsl/wsl.go`. Only tests call it, so the guard failed the
  last slice, as the vertical rule wants. The fix session got the
  v0.0.14 text "This slice wrote a duplicate … Do not delete or rename
  the earlier code". It changed correct code and stopped at
  `error_max_turns`. The correct repair moves the helper into
  `wsl_test.go`, and the text of #148 forbids that too. The branch
  `minion/implement-implement-55` (`3a20084`) holds slice 1, and no PR
  exists.
- **Open at 06:34Z on 10-24 (Q7).** The pick: a cli rule (a helper that
  only tests use goes in a `_test.go` file of its package), a change
  of the guard text in minions, and v0.0.15 (it also ships #147 and
  #148) with the pin bump in the 8 cli workflows. Then delete the
  branch again and comment `/minion build`; the plan can stay. Also
  open: a new issue for the Linux `sanitizePath` bug, the vertical rule
  in `/code-create-issues`, and the turn limit of the fact-checker.

name: Run Minion

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      program:
        description: "Program .md file path (e.g., .minions/programs/detect-hooks.md)"
        required: true
        type: string
      dry_run:
        description: "Dry run (prompt generation only)"
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

  issues:
    types: [labeled]

  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

# Each minion agent call runs Claude Code on the runner VM. These two
# values choose its model and its effort. Opus 5.5 needs Claude Code
# 2.1.280 or newer on the runner.
env:
  ANTHROPIC_MODEL: claude-opus-5-5
  CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL: high

jobs:
  run-minion:
    # A comment starts a build only when the command opens it and a trusted
    # account wrote it. The repository is public, so anyone can comment, and
    # the build runs on the self-hosted runner with GH_PAT. The review posts
    # its own comments as the operator, so a quote of the command inside a
    # comment must not start a build either.
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && (github.event.label.name == 'minion-ready' || github.event.label.name == 'minion-approved')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
       startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/minion build') &&
       contains(fromJSON('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association))
    runs-on: github-runner-partio-minion-ai-01
    timeout-minutes: 180

    # The pattern partio-minions uses to find the slice-plan comment
    # (internal/slices/slices.go, planMarkerRe). Two steps below read it, and
    # a build that reads a different pattern than the runtime is a build that
    # researches a planned issue, or builds an unplanned one.
    #
    # The review session writes its verdict to MINION_REVIEW_DIR. It runs in
    # an isolated minions worktree, so the path is absolute, in this
    # workspace, where the gate step finds it.
    env:
      MINION_REVIEW_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.minion-review
      SLICE_PLAN_MARKER: '^[[:space:]]*<!--[[:space:]]*minion:research-slices([[:space:]][^>]*)?-->[[:space:]]*$'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Determine program
        id: program
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "path=${{ inputs.program }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "dry_run=${{ inputs.dry_run }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "issue_num=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            ISSUE_NUM="${{ github.event.issue.number }}"
            echo "path=.minions/programs/implement.md" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "dry_run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "issue_num=${ISSUE_NUM}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi


      - name: Install minions
        run: |
          go install github.com/partio-io/minions/cmd/minions@v0.0.15
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # The issue is reviewed before the build starts, not inside it, with
      # the program and gate the sweep uses. The runtime creates the branch
      # before the agent session runs and pushes unconditionally, so a build
      # that stops partway still leaves a branch and a pull request behind.
      # Stopping here leaves neither.
      #
      # The verdict decides, not the session: a crashed session must not end
      # the job before the gate fails it closed.
      - name: Review the issue
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}
        run: |
          rm -rf "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR"
          mkdir -p "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR"
          minions run .minions/programs/review.md --issue "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"

      # The gate acts on the verdict and writes two outputs. blocked is true
      # after a close: the gate's comment explains it, and nothing below
      # runs. changed is true after a rewrite: the old slice plan describes
      # the old text, so research runs again. No verdict exits 1 and fails
      # the job, and the failure step marks the issue.
      - name: Review gate
        id: gate
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          go run ./cmd/minion-review gate --mode build \
            --issue "${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}" \
            --verdict "$MINION_REVIEW_DIR/verdict.json"

      # A slice plan is the contract between research and the build. The
      # runtime reads the latest comment that carries the marker and builds
      # one slice per session; when no comment carries it, the build falls
      # back to a single unplanned session without a word on the issue
      # (internal/executor/slice.go, resolveSlicePlan). Detect the plan with
      # the pattern the runtime itself uses, so the two never disagree.
      #
      # A rewrite voids the plan the issue carries. The step then records
      # the time, after the rewrite, so the confirmation below accepts only a
      # plan that research publishes from now on.
      - name: Look for a slice plan
        id: slices
        if: steps.program.outputs.issue_num != '' && steps.gate.outputs.blocked != 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: |
          ISSUE_NUM="${{ steps.program.outputs.issue_num }}"

cb605ba Put helpers that only tests use in test files
On issue 55 the PRD copied a pattern from its prior art: an unexported
resetCache() in production code, so that tests can reset a cache.
Slice 1 put it in internal/wsl/wsl.go. Only tests called it, so the
slice boundary guard failed the last slice, and the fix session could
not repair it.

A helper that only tests use belongs in a _test.go file of the same
package: that file can reach the unexported state, and production code
then holds no code that only tests call. The rule now stands in three
places:

1. prd-writer: Testing Decisions say where such a helper lives, also
   when the prior art puts it in production code.
2. slicer: the vertical rule puts such a helper in the test file.
3. implement: a slice puts such a helper in a _test.go file.

A dry run of both programs shows the new text in the prompts.

content.text:
Issue 43 failed because GitHub refused the push. Slice 3 put its workflow template in `.github/workflows/`, and the build token is not allowed to write there.

**What happened**
- Failed run: https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/44044521896 (CI fail, 2026-11-17)
- Issue: https://github.com/partio-io/cli/issues/43 (open, label `minion-failed`)
- Slices 1 and 2 passed and are on the remote branch `minion/implement-implement-43`, at `e887233`. There is no PR.
- Slice 3 built the workflow template and the README section. Then the push failed:
  ```
  refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml.example` without `workflows` permission
  ```
- GitHub applies this check to every file under `.github/workflows/`, also a `.yml.example` file. The error names a GitHub App, so I think the push used the `GITHUB_TOKEN` that `actions/checkout` keeps. A `permissions:` setting cannot give that token write access to workflow files. I did not check this in the minions code.
- The slice 3 work is gone, because the runner worktree was deleted.
- The run cost $3.85.

**Cause in the pipeline:** the research plan put the template under `.github/workflows/`. No rule in `research.md` or `implement.md` stops a plan or a slice from writing a file there.

Defaults that I set. Tell me if one is wrong:
- The new path for the template is `docs/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml`. A file outside `.github/workflows/` never runs, so it does not need the `.example` suffix.
- If the new rule tells implement to change the plan's path, the re-run can keep the branch and continue at slice 3 with the current plan. That costs about $0.70 and needs no new research.

❓ **Q1** - **How to fix the pipeline**: Do we add a rule that keeps minions out of `.github/workflows/`, or do we let minion pushes write workflow files?

➡️ Add the rule, in the same 3 places as the rule from commit `cb605ba`: prd-writer, slicer and implement. The issue text is public and the runner is self-hosted. A minion that can push a live workflow file could then run any code with the repo secrets, so the GitHub check is a guard to keep. The other choice is a PAT with the `workflow` scope for the push.

Reply: "yes" to take the pick, or answer by number.

## main...origin/main
83cd78e Merge pull request #834 from partio-io/minion/implement-implement-41
### prd-writer

```capabilities
tools:
  - Read
  - Write
  - Bash
max_turns: 20
```

Before anything else, read the premise verdict and stop unless it
passed:

```
PREMISE="/tmp/minion-research-premise-${MINION_ISSUE_NUMBER:-0}.md"
head -1 "$PREMISE"
```

If that first line is not exactly `PREMISE_OK`, the premise-checker
blocked this run. Write no PRD and stop immediately.

You synthesize the completed research transcript into a PRD body. You
do NOT interview, ask questions, or modify the transcript — the
researcher and persona have already produced it. Your job is pure
synthesis: read the Q&A, decide what the PRD says, write the PRD.

PRD shape (mirrors the `/code-create-prd` skill — section headings may
be tuned but the general structure must hold):

1. `## Problem Statement` — the problem from the user's perspective.
2. `## Solution` — the solution from the user's perspective.
3. `## User Stories` — a long, numbered list in the form
   "As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>".
4. `## Implementation Decisions` — modules built or modified, module
   interfaces, architectural decisions, schema/API contracts, specific

content.text: Each of the 3 slice prompts and the research prompt now carry the rule. Commit, push, PR:

input.command:
git add .minions/programs/implement.md .minions/programs/research.md && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Keep minion builds out of .github/workflows

On issue 43 the PRD put a workflow template at
.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml.example. Slice 3 wrote it, and
GitHub refused the push: "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or
update workflow ... without `workflows` permission". GitHub applies
this check to each file under .github/workflows/, also a .yml.example
file. The build failed at slice 3 of 3, and its work was lost.

We keep the GitHub check. The issue text is public and the runner is
self-hosted, so a build that can push a live workflow file can run
any code with the repo secrets. A workflow template now lives under
docs/workflows/. The rule stands in three places:

1. prd-writer: Implementation Decisions put a template under
   docs/workflows/ and never plan a change to a live workflow file.
2. slicer: no slice touches .github/workflows/; a PRD path there
   becomes a docs/workflows/ path in the slice text.
3. implement: never touch .github/workflows/, also when the issue or
   the plan names a path there; the PR description says where the
   template is.

A dry run of both programs on issue 43 shows the new text in the
prompts of all three slices and of research.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin argos/no-minion-workflow-files 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --repo partio-io/cli --base main --head argos/no-minion-workflow-files --title "Keep minion builds out of .github/workflows" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Problem

The minion build of https://github.com/partio-io/cli/issues/43 failed at slice 3 of 3:
https://github.com/partio-io/cli/actions/runs/44044521896

The PRD put a workflow template at `.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml.example`. GitHub refused the push:

```
refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/partio-sync-fork.yml.example` without `workflows` permission
```

GitHub applies this check to each file under `.github/workflows/`, also a `.yml.example` file.

## Change

We keep the GitHub check. The issue text is public and the runner is self-hosted. A build that can push a live workflow file can run any code with the repo secrets.

A workflow template now lives under `docs/workflows/`. The rule stands in three places:

1. `prd-writer` (`research.md`): Implementation Decisions put a template under `docs/workflows/`.
2. `slicer` (`research.md`): no slice touches `.github/workflows/`. A PRD path there becomes a `docs/workflows/` path.
3. `implement` (`implement.md`): never touch `.github/workflows/`, also when the issue or the plan names a path there.

## Test

`minions run <program> --issue 43 --dry-run` for `implement.md` and `research.md`. The new text is in the prompts of all three slices and of research.

## After the merge

The branch `minion/implement-implement-43` keeps slices 1 and 2. A `/minion build` comment on issue 43 continues at slice 3 with the current plan. The implement rule moves the template to `docs/workflows/`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
